gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the BIQU CryoGrip Pro Frostbite's AR code is read only by the Bambu X1C, so A1, P1, P2 and X2D owners must turn off Build Plate Detection, or that the 256/257 mm Bambu-size plates do not fit the H2 series, which needs a separate 350 × 325 mm size.
standout_why: I compared against nozzlenotes.com/articles/printers/3d-printer-build-plates (top result). It names no plate-to-printer fit, gives no sizes and says nothing about plate detection; its only Bambu note is that some entries do not apply to the A1 mini. I also compared 3dadapt.com/guides/smooth-textured-satin-build-plates, which covers only Prusa MK4/MK4S sheets and says it 'does not establish compatibility for similarly named third-party plates … or other printer models'. The cited Prusa guidepost (help.prusa3d.com flexible-steel-sheets) maps sheets only to Prusa families and says the HighTemp sheet is for the HT90 only. ChatGPT's own answer stopped at 'What 3D printer do you have?' None of these covers Bambu plate sizes, plate detection or third-party plate recognition.
decides: It confirms the current picks and adds a per-printer fit row rather than changing the winner. Frostbite (the cold-PLA pick) and the Bambu SuperTack both come in a 256/257 mm size for A1, P1, X1, P2S and X2D. The 257 mm plates will not fit the H2 series (H2D, H2S, H2C), which needs a 350 × 325 mm plate (BIQU's H-series PyroGrip is 346 × 355 mm). On every printer except the X1C, plan to turn off Build Plate Detection, because the plate's AR or QR code is not read there.
